evidence.quote: Taking into account the downside risks at a time when inflation is on the soft side would argue for softening the expected path of monetary policy according to basic principles of risk management.
Over the past year, inflation has fallen short of the Federal Reserve's 2 percent objective, and that has been the case more often than not in recent years.
Indeed, some indicators of longer-run inflation expectations have been on the soft side in recent months.
Recent data suggest the economy is growing solidly. Consumer spending is robust, buoyed by the strong labor market and continued strong confidence.
While the modal outlook is solid, the downside risks, if they materialize, could weigh on economic activity.
